name: Harmondsworth Moor
highlights: 260 acres of reclaimed land turned into wildlife habitat by British Airways, with rolling hills and great limestone trails minutes from Heathrow.

name: Cranford Country Park
highlights: A historic estate park with the stables, walls and church of a lost manor house set among open grassland, woodland and the River Crane.

name: Stockley & Lake Farm Country Parks
highlights: Two west London green spaces with brilliant gravel and limestone trails looping a golf course, with easy access to the Grand Union Canal.

name: Horsenden Hill
waypoints: Grand Union Canal Paddington Branch Perivale
highlights: The largest conservation site in the Borough of Ealing and a top off-road spot, with great views from its wooded summit.

name: Ruislip Woods
highlights: The ideal weekend long run through 300-plus hectares of stunning woodland around a sparkling lake, with a lazy lakeside lunch to follow.

name: Fryent Country Park
highlights: A dose of English countryside on a hill in the middle of suburban London, with a stellar view of Wembley Stadium.

name: Canons Park
highlights: Former estate grounds restored in 2006, offering formal gardens, a historic walled garden and temple, and woodland walks in a compact space.

name: Southall Park
highlights: Formal parkland with rolling undulations and handy distance markers on its perimeter, ideal for speed sessions.

name: Walpole & Lammas Parks
highlights: Two beautifully presented parks - Walpole with Pitzhanger Manor and a pond, Lammas with a big grass field - linked into a figure-of-eight.

name: Hanger Hill Park & Fox Wood
highlights: A hilly green pairing of Hanger Hill Park's sealed circuit with Fox Wood's wooded trails and stairs, extendable to nearby Pitshanger Park.

name: Chiswick House Gardens
highlights: A small but stunning park with grand vistas, a mirror-like lake and formal gardens that inspired parks worldwide, just 400m from the Thames.

name: Gunnersbury Park
highlights: Two old mansions and huge grass sports fields ringed by sealed and dirt trails, with ponds, a Gothic tower and a secret garden to discover.

name: Muswell Hill Playing Fields
highlights: A connectable mix of woods, playing fields and a large cemetery giving nice, largely off-road running.

name: Waterlow Park
highlights: A little but stunning hillside park with formal gardens, great views and a chain of ponds, a short stroll from Hampstead Heath.

name: The Parks of Pymmes Brook
highlights: Three riverside parks strung along the Pymmes Brook, with striking brick railway arches and lots of extra trails on a there-and-back run.

name: Monken Hadley Common
highlights: A long stretch of woodland marking the border between suburban London and open countryside, with hills and a pretty fishing lake.

name: Trent Country Park
highlights: A former royal hunting ground and grand estate of undulating hills, woodlands, lakes and an Obelisk, in a safe enclosed setting.

name: Celandine Route
highlights: An 11-mile point-to-point tracing the way-marked Celandine Route along the River Pinn through sleepy outer northwest suburbs to the Grand Union Canal.

name: Brent River Park Footpath
highlights: A largely traffic-free point-to-point along the River Brent through many of Ealing's best parks, passing under the 1837 Wharncliffe Viaduct.

name: Dollis Valley Greenwalk
highlights: A 13-mile way-marked point-to-point through Barnet's green spaces, following the Dollis Brook past a huge Victorian viaduct.

name: Grand Union Canal: Paddington Branch
highlights: More than a half-marathon of uninterrupted canal towpath from Little Venice all the way west to Hayes - a bucket-list running accomplishment.
